# Clone protocol docs reject the omission required by environment clones

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

The shared clone-request documentation tells future callers that a missing target host is only tolerated to decode and refuse old requests. In this change, cloning a sandbox or container requires exactly that missing host. Following the documented contract would construct a request that the new environment path rejects. This is an internal documentation defect, not a runtime acceptance bug.

## Details

At crates/farhelm-proto/src/lib.rs:2064-2066, Clone is described as copying onto an explicitly named host. At 2077-2078, host says: 'The target host's display NAME. `None` is retained only so an old wire shape can be decoded and refused.' The complete contract added by the reviewed commit contradicts that exclusivity: SPEC.md:4327-4328 says '`farhelm agent clone` of a sandbox or container session takes no `--host` or `--cwd`; it targets the source's recipe at the source's place, with the source's launch and repository intent, never a copy of its disk.'

The executable boundary agrees with the new product contract. The same commit changes ParsedAgentVerb::Clone.host from required to optional and routes a session-owned source through clone_environment_for_agent before requiring a host for ordinary clone. At agent_requests.rs:4316-4321, any Some(host) is refused for an environment clone; absent host continues through source validation and launch_environment_for_agent at 4368-4390. Thus omission is current supported intent, not merely legacy wire tolerance. Document the two cases: ordinary clone requires the named target host, while environment clone omits it and retains source recipe/place. The top-level Clone summary should carry the same exception.

Attribution was checked over the whole pinned range. Exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a already had the quoted host wording, which was then true for its ordinary-clone-only path. The 190d844e parent-to-child agent_requests.rs patch introduces the optional parse and early environment branch, making the unchanged protocol comment newly false inside the assigned range. Range endpoint 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db retains the same host comment at lib.rs:1954-1955. The correct production refusal is not a refutation of this separately misleading documentation.

Confidence: confirmed from pinned source, introducing behavior patch, exact product contract and endpoint check; no runtime observation or reproduction. # Shared template-context docs still exclude all agent recipe catalogs

Reviewed behavior commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

The shared template API tells maintainers that agent callers supply no recipes, although the new agent-launch implementation must supply them, even for an ordinary create whose last template selects an existing host. Following the documented rule would make a valid template stack fail. This is inaccurate internal caller-contract documentation; current execution supplies the catalogs correctly.

## Details

At crates/farhelm-proto/src/launcher.rs:600-602 the known_recipes field says 'Saved recipe names the caller can launch. Agent callers supply no recipes; GUI callers use their current catalog rather than guessing.' Agent calls now reach exactly this shared API with recipes. agent_launch.rs:233-238 constructs TemplateContext from placement.known_recipes/known_places. agent_requests.rs:2447-2475 explicitly loads the saved recipe catalog and place IDs for ordinary non-spawn creates, then passes them through resolve_placed. Its comment explains the non-obvious reason: a recipe template may appear before a later installed-host template, so the earlier recipe must still be applicable even though the final create uses an ordinary host. Empty recipes would cause the shared fold's known_recipes check to refuse that valid earlier template. The explicit environment-create path also needs this catalog. Spawn retains the restricted empty-catalog path through agent_launch::resolve at 145-151. The field contract should describe caller-supplied admissible recipes and distinguish restricted spawn from fleet agent creation; it must not classify all agent callers together.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md Agent requests and environments at 6677-6682 permits plain creates whose named template targets a recipe to use the environment path; the same section and shared-template contract preserve ordinary template application semantics. The new resolve_placed contract at agent_launch.rs:176-180 explicitly requires knowledge of both installs and recipes because later placement replaces earlier placement. Correct production behavior does not refute the independently false shared-API explanation.

Full-range attribution: the exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a already has this sentence at launcher.rs:588-589, while agent resolution still hardcodes empty recipe/place slices. The complete range history through 190d844e finds only that behavior commit changing those resolver inputs; its parent-to-child patch changes TemplateContext construction from known_recipes:&[] to placement.known_recipes and adds resolve_placed. Thus the new behavior makes the old statement false inside the assigned range. Pinned endpoint 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db retains the same sentence at launcher.rs:600-601.

Suggested bucket: other, internal API documentation. Confidence: confirmed pinned-source, actual caller construction, introducing behavior patch and endpoint comparison; no runtime evidence. Could-be-highest: no established security or user-work-loss route. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: supplied g018/f2 reports the same incorrect agent-catalog distinction in helm Placement documentation plus a separate unresolved helper link. This is an additional assigned proto-field manifestation requiring its own wording change, not a claimed new independent runtime/root-cause issue; parent owns consolidation. Caveats: do not remove the legitimate empty-catalog restriction from spawn, and do not imply recipe catalogs alone grant environment-launch approval. All readily checkable premises resolved; l8 is closed as this documentation finding. No test, build or reproduction.

# Environment creating replies can substitute a replacement connection claim

Reviewed commit: 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435

## TLDR

After creating a new sandbox or container session, the agent can receive an earlier connection's result marked fresh under a connection that replaced it before reply projection. The create still succeeded and the session reference still names the same entry. The issue is inaccurate freshness metadata, not physical retargeting, execution on another machine or loss of work. This corroborates caller-owned g020/l8 event29, not a newly independent discovery.

## Details

Read the complete 19-event local findings history and ONLY the named g020/l8 event29 before synthesis. Independently checked the exact protocol/caller boundary: proto/lib.rs:2640-2644 allows host_id to retain the original entry UUID even for a stale result, while 2648-2658 explicitly includes every mutating reply and the creating verbs in the actual-routed-connection contract. It says the row's host 'is pinned to the connection the mutation actually routed through' and that when that connection is no longer current, host=None accompanies stale. New CreateEnvironment is expressly answered with AgentReply::Created at 2092-2095; the new caller uses agent_created_reply, whose 4662-4680 documentation and implementation share the ordinary mutation projection. No new environment freshness exception is encoded or documented in this representation.

The narrow data-flow checks independently reproduce g020's source conclusion without execution. sessions.rs:1844-1866 captures the real claim/client before a managed-checkout create and returns that same claim, and the ordinary branch returns it at 1923. But create_in_session_sandbox at 1793-1794 keeps only the qualified SessionInfo and discards the claim. The provisioning completion at tensorlake_add.rs:1018-1026 awaits step publication and a memory lock, then sends only this session result at 1057. The new agent caller samples host_client AFTER receiving the result (agent_requests.rs:4578-4588), using either the current claim or an invalid sentinel only if no client exists. Its existing projection at 4694-4707 compares that sampled claim's incarnation with the current snapshot, which can match a replacement connection and report host:Some/current name with stale:false for earlier data.

Connection replacement is distinct from logical entry identity: manager.rs:5190-5207 explicitly mints a fresh incarnation whenever the client changes, including disappearance; refreshes on one client keep their incarnation. Provisioning releases the environment's connection hold before attach_supervisor (tensorlake_add.rs:612-614); the later result boundary retains neither original claim nor connection lease. The separately owned completion and agent-receiver tasks and intervening awaited bookkeeping permit reconnect before the receiver samples its new claim. Source supports this conditional interleaving; no occurrence, timing frequency or destructive consequence was observed. The correct remedy is to retain the actual mutation claim through the owned result and project against it, or conservatively mark the result stale if that evidence is unavailable. Stable reference qualification alone cannot recreate freshness evidence.

Contract reconciliation: SPEC.md logical-host approvals and c3's pending container-place authority uncertainty concern what an approved operation may target. They do not define the incarnation freshness of a completed reply. A permitted stable entry/reference and successful create can coexist with host=None/stale for the old connection. Therefore neither accepting logical-entry targeting nor c3's direct-Allow source refutations settles or drops this separate freshness defect. No new highest consequence is inferred.

Suggested bucket: other (agent reply accuracy). Confidence: confirmed conditional source/data-flow and shared-contract mismatch; no runtime observation. Could-be-highest: false on this record; no physical target change, credential exposure, reference misrouting, security or user-work-loss route alleged. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: exact g020/l8 event29 owns the complete caller defect and range-attribution/persistence evidence; this is the assigned protocol interface corroboration for consolidation, not a second independent runtime finding or a new false-doc-only report. Caveats: an environment still disconnected at projection uses the stale sentinel as intended; the problem requires a replacement connection current before projection. Ordinary creation remains subject to the same shared freshness contract. Prior c3 highest conditional consequence, both competing authority clauses, its investigated scope uncertainty and all proposals remain unchanged. All readily checkable protocol-scope/result-boundary premises resolved; l9 is closed as this corroborating finding. No tests, builds, reproductions, unrelated search, forbidden coverage reads, checkout edits, nested agents or live actions.
